Larder

BestBefore should feel like a well-kept larder: oat paper, bottle green and a hearty book serif. Three rules guide every screen. Tell people what to use first in plain words. Keep colour for food that needs attention, so fresh food stays quiet. Treat a passed date as a fact to deal with, never a failure.

Colour primitives

Raw ramps. Screens never use these directly, only through the semantic roles below.

Semantic roles

What screens use, per theme. The expired, today and soon roles exist so food status can change without touching error colours.

Contrast (WCAG 2.2 AA)

Every pair the components use. Text needs 4.5:1, large text and UI parts 3:1. Generated by the build, so it can't drift from the tokens.

Typography

Vollkorn carries headings and covers Latin and Cyrillic. Body text uses the platform font: Roboto on Android, SF Pro on iOS. All sizes scale with the system text size.

Срокоед · Греческий йогурт

Matvakt · Blåbær og rømme

Spacing

Shape

Elevation

Only floating things get a shadow: Scan, snackbars, sheets and dialogs. Lists sit on the page with a hairline.

Icons

Lucide at 1.75 stroke. Category icons stand in when a product has no photo.

Illustrations

Only in empty states. One family: a thin line over soft shapes, no characters.

Expiry status

The app's most important component. Colour appears only when food needs attention. Every status has an icon and words, so it never depends on colour.

Past-date wording stays factual: "1 day over", never "Expired!" or "Wasted". Read aloud as "Sourdough bread, one day past its date".

Pantry row

Name, then status, then where it lives. Quantity sits at the end. Tapping opens the product. Rows stay one line each and truncate; the full name is on the detail sheet.

Row height at least 68dp. Swipe actions have a visible equivalent on the detail sheet, so nothing depends on a gesture.

Button

One primary button per view. Labels are verbs that say what happens: "Save to Fridge", not "OK".

Touch target at least 48dp on Android and 44pt on iOS. Loading keeps the button width so nothing jumps.

Text field

Always a visible label. Validate when the field loses focus.

Selection controls

Chips filter and pick one place. The round tick marks something done, and also appears on the shopping widget. Switches change a setting straight away.

Dialog, sheet, card

Dialogs are for decisions only. Sheets hold filters, sort and product details.

Empty state and loading

Pantry data is on the device, so lists open instantly with no skeletons. Loading indicators belong only to barcode lookup, receipts and image reads.

Error and feedback framework

Every message lands on exactly one surface. Walk these in order and stop at the first match.

  1. Must the person decide, or is it irreversible? T6 dialog.
  2. Tied to one input? T1 field error.
  3. Can the screen's content not be shown at all? T5 screen error.
  4. Does the condition last? T4 callout.
  5. Otherwise it's an event: T3 snackbar.

Reversible actions (use, toss or remove one item) happen straight away with Undo. Dialogs are for irreversible actions and real choices.

App icon direction

The icon moves from teal to bottle green: a preserving jar with a paper label, keeping the old icon's jar idea. Final artwork comes at implementation.

App shell

Four destinations: Home, Recipe, Shopping and Settings. Scan is always one tap away on Home. Every device uses the same floating pill bar, on Android and iOS. Tablets and foldables get two panes where the content earns them, and the pill stays at the bottom so it never takes a column.

BestBefore

Home

Screen content sits here. Scroll areas leave room for Scan, so nothing hides behind it.

HomeRecipe5ShoppingSettings

Native behaviour per platform

One look, native behaviour. These parts follow each platform.

ElementAndroid (Material 3)iOS and iPadOS (HIG)
NavigationFloating pill bar on phones, tablets and foldablesThe same floating pill bar, on iPad too
ScanExtended FAB above the pill on phones, level with it at the bottom right on tabletsSame button and position, respecting the safe area
BackSystem back and predictive backEdge swipe and back chevron
SheetsModal bottom sheetSheet with medium and large detents
DialogsAlert dialog, buttons as designedNative alert; destructive role on the confirm action
Date pickerMaterial date pickerWheel date picker, kept on purpose because people got stuck in the graphical one
Swipe on a rowSwipe to dismiss with a coloured revealNative swipe actions
Snackbar with UndoSnackbarSame component, as iOS has no native equivalent
Body fontRobotoSF Pro
Text sizeFollows font scaleFollows Dynamic Type, Vollkorn scaled with it

Onboarding

Four short screens, then the pantry. Each permission is explained just before the system asks, and nothing depends on the answer. New to the app: today Android and iOS both ask for notifications on first launch with no explanation.

BestBefore

Reminds you before food goes off, not after.

Private by design

No account and no ads. Your pantry stays on your device.

A quiet nudge, the day before

We remind you at 09:00, the day before a date. You can change the time or turn reminders off in Settings.

Scan it instead of typing

Ready for your first item

Bring something from the fridge and scan it. It takes a few seconds.

You can start without them

Everything else works. You can change your mind at any time.

  • Reminders are off

  • The camera is off

Pantry

Home answers one question in plain words: what should I use first? The sentence at the top changes with the food, the list keeps the soonest dates first, and Scan is the one primary action. Tapping a row shows what is in the product and everything you can do with it.

How the Home sentence is chosen

The lede always describes the whole pantry, whatever filter is on. Walk these in order and stop at the first match. Numbers up to ten are words, then digits. Russian needs plural forms for one, few and many.

Pantry holdsLedeVariant
2 or more due by tomorrowThree things to use by tomorrowPlural. Past-date items count
1 due by tomorrowOne thing to use by tomorrowSingular
2 or more past their date, nothing today or tomorrowTwo things are past their dateOverdue, plural
1 past its date, nothing today or tomorrowOne thing is past its dateOverdue, singular
Nothing by tomorrow, something within 7 daysNext up: Semi-skimmed milk on FridayCalm, names the next item
Nothing within 7 daysNothing needs using this weekCalm
No itemsNo lede. The empty state speaksFirst use

Add item

One form for adding and editing. It opens from a scan or by hand and has one job: save the item with the right date. The date gets its own card, and Save stays pinned above the keyboard, so typing a name and saving takes no scrolling.

Scanner

Full screen over the camera, with no tab bar. One bar at the bottom picks how to capture: Barcode, Batch, Receipt, Date or Photo. Close, the torch and Type it in stay on screen, so there is always a way out that doesn't need the camera.

The camera stays dark

The picture, its controls and the mode bar are dark in both themes, because a bright interface around a live picture dazzles and hides what the camera sees. They use the dark values of the normal roles, so nothing new enters the palette. Result panels and dialogs follow the theme.

The picture can be any brightness, so text on it always sits on the scrim at 72%. With a white packet behind it, on-surface still reaches 6.3:1. On-surface-variant only reaches 4.1:1 there, so it isn't used on the picture. The aiming frame has a light ring and a dark ring, so one of them always clears 3:1. Pictures on this page are drawn stand-ins.

A menu for three days is written by the server only. This tab replaces Calendar.

Recipe

Spinach and yoghurt eggs on sourdough toast

A warm, quick plate that uses the bread, the spinach and one of the yoghurts today.

15 min2 servingsEasy

Ingredients

  • 4 slicesSourdough breadIn your pantry
  • 100 gBaby spinachIn your pantry
  • 150 gGreek yoghurtIn your pantry
  • 4Free-range eggsIn your pantry
  • 1 cloveGarlic
  • 1 tbspOlive oil
  • Salt, pepper, chilli flakes

Method

  1. 1

    Stir the grated garlic and a pinch of salt into the yoghurt and leave it at room temperature.

  2. 2

    Toast the bread. Day-old sourdough toasts better than fresh.

  3. 3

    Warm the oil in a pan, add the spinach and turn it for a minute until it wilts. Season.

  4. 4

    Fry or poach the eggs to your liking.

  5. 5

    Spread the yoghurt on the toast, pile on the spinach, top with the eggs and finish with chilli flakes.

TipCheck the bread before using it: one day past a best-before date is usually fine, but not if there is any mould.

Written by our server · Saved on this phone

  • 100 gBaby spinachIn your pantry
  • 150 gGreek yoghurtIn your pantry

  • 1 cloveGarlic

Method

  1. 1

  2. 2

Recipe

Slow-roasted salmon with spinach, yoghurt and sourdough crumb, served with a warm strawberry and black pepper salad

A longer cook for a weekend, using the salmon before Saturday along with the bread, the spinach, both yoghurts and the strawberries.

1 h 10 min4 servingsAmbitious

Ingredients

  • 2Salmon filletIn your pantry
  • 4 slicesSourdough bread, blitzed to coarse crumbsIn your pantry
  • 100 gBaby spinachIn your pantry
  • 300 gGreek yoghurtIn your pantry
  • 250 gStrawberriesIn your pantry
  • 1Unwaxed lemon, zest and juice
  • 2 clovesGarlic
  • 3 tbspOlive oil
  • 1 tspCoarsely ground black pepper
  • Flaky salt

Method

  1. 1

    Heat the oven to 120°C. Line a tray and bring the salmon out of the fridge twenty minutes before cooking so it cooks evenly.

  2. 2

    Toss the crumbs with two tablespoons of oil, the garlic and the lemon zest. Toast in a dry pan over a medium heat, stirring, until deep gold. This takes about eight minutes; do not walk away from it.

  3. 3

    Season the salmon, lay it skin down on the tray and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until it flakes under gentle pressure but is still glossy in the middle.

  4. 4

    Halve the strawberries, warm them in a pan with the remaining oil and the pepper for two minutes, then add a squeeze of lemon.

  5. 5

    Fold the spinach through the yoghurt with a pinch of salt.

  6. 6

    Spoon the yoghurt on to plates, lay the salmon on top, scatter over the crumbs and serve the strawberries alongside.

TipLow oven temperatures vary. If the salmon still looks raw after 30 minutes, give it five more rather than turning the heat up.

Three routes, one form

The form and the ticked items feed all three routes. What differs is where the writing happens and what it costs. What a recipe and a menu take comes from our server with every count, so it can change without an app update; the apps show 1, 4 and 5 until they first hear from it.

RouteCostLeaves the phoneResultNeeds
Recipe from a pack1 recipeItem names, dates and the form, to our serverIn the app, savedConnection, a pack
Menu for 3 days4 recipes with 2 courses a day, 5 with 3The sameIn the app, saved as one entryConnection, a pack
On this phoneFreeNothingIn the app, savedA phone with its own model, in a language it knows
PromptFreeOnly what the person sharesIn the other appNothing

Ways in

The Recipe tab opens with the soonest items ticked. Get recipe ideas in Home's multi-select and the Recipe ideas action on a reminder open it with those items ticked instead. Neither writes anything by itself: the person still chooses a route.

When a recipe is taken

Only for something delivered, with one limit. A recipe or menu is held when Generate is tapped. If our side fails or times out, it is always given back; after several such failures in one day the server stops writing until the next day, and the app says to try again later. If the request itself fails, because the model refuses it or it comes back incomplete (a menu missing a day or a course is incomplete), it is given back a limited number of times: one for every ten recipes bought. After that such a failure counts, and the snackbar says how many recipes were taken. Retrying after a lost connection never takes a second one. The count on screen changes when the result appears.

Shopping

What do I need to buy? One field adds by typing or by scan, sections follow the way you walk the shop, and the round tick takes things off as you go. Lists travel by text or QR code, because nothing leaves the phone otherwise.

Settings

Everything sits on one page, grouped by the question it answers: when the app reminds you, how it knows your kitchen, how it looks, and where your data is. Choices save as they are made, so there is no Save button. Tablets split the page into a section list with its current values, and one section beside it.

Widgets and notifications

What people see outside the app. Widgets answer "what do I use first" and "what do I need" at a glance. Notifications stay calm: a reminder is a piece of information, never an alarm. Theme comes from the toggle above, and both platforms share a frame so they can be compared.

Notification copy

The current titles conflict with the no-alarm brief, and the bodies break the no-exclamation rule. Russian and Norwegian are drafts for translator review. Title and body keys also exist in iOS Localizable.strings, so changing them touches six files. Fallback and channel strings are Android only. Plural forms are shown once.
